title: The Conference of the Birds
author: Farid ad-Din Attar (Masani)
description: The Conference of the Birds (Mantiq al-Tayr) by Farid ud-Din Attar (c. 1145-1221), the Persian Sufi poet of Nishapur, in the English version by R. P. Masani (Oxford University Press, 1924), a prose rendering and study of the poem's Sufi teaching. In this allegorical epic the birds of the world gather to seek their king, the Simorgh. Led by the hoopoe, they voice their excuses and attachments, the nightingale its love of the rose and the parrot its desire for immortality, which the hoopoe answers with stories. They journey through seven valleys: quest, love, knowledge, detachment, unity, bewilderment, and poverty and annihilation. Only thirty birds (si murgh) survive to reach the Simorgh, where they discover that the Simorgh is themselves. A supreme classic of Sufi literature, it influenced Rumi and is read as a map of the mystical path.
